title: Comparing the Graphs and Behavior of y = tan x and y = cot x
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph y = \tan x and y = \cot x together over the interval -7 \le x \le 7. Explain how the behavior of \cot x relates to the signs, zeros, asymptotes, and monotonicity of \tan x.
finalAnswer: \cot x = \frac{1}{\tan x} \text{ shares the sign of } \tan x, \text{ turns zeros of } \tan x \text{ into asymptotes (and vice versa), and decreases where } \tan x \text{ increases}

steps.title: Compare Signs and Intersection Points
steps.mathExpression: \cot x = \frac{1}{\tan x}, \quad \tan x = \cot x \iff \tan^2 x = 1 \iff x = \frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{k\pi}{2}
steps.explanation: Because cot x = 1/tan x, both functions have the exact same sign in every quadrant. Their graphs intersect wherever tan x = cot x = +/-1, which occurs at odd multiples of pi/4.
steps.why: A nonzero number and its reciprocal have the same sign and are equal if and only if the number is 1 or -1.

steps.title: Compare Zeros and Vertical Asymptotes
steps.mathExpression: \tan(k\pi) = 0 \iff x = k\pi \text{ is a vertical asymptote of } \cot x; \quad \cot\left(\frac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\right) = 0 \iff x = \frac{\pi}{2} + k\pi \text{ is an asymptote of } \tan x
steps.explanation: At every x-intercept of tan x (x = 0, +/-pi, +/-2*pi inside [-7, 7]), cot x has a vertical asymptote. Conversely, at every vertical asymptote of tan x (x = +/-pi/2, +/-3*pi/2), cot x crosses the x-axis at 0.
steps.why: Since tan x = sin x / cos x and cot x = cos x / sin x, the zeros of the numerator of one are the zeros of the denominator of the other.

steps.title: Compare Monotonicity and Cofunction Shift
steps.explanation: While tan x is strictly increasing on each open interval between its asymptotes, its reciprocal cot x is strictly decreasing on each open interval between its asymptotes.
steps.why: If a positive or negative function u(x) is strictly increasing, its reciprocal 1/u(x) is strictly decreasing on the same interval.
